title: Chow module with finite cohomology and generic rank one
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $T$ affine and $R=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ Noetherian, and $i:W\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $W$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Put $\eta=\operatorname{genericPoint}(W)$ and $\xi=i(\eta)$. There exists a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$ [pqf-def-coherent] whose support, the nonzero-stalk locus [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], is $i(W)$, whose stalk $G_\xi$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_\xi$, and which admits a $\kappa(\xi)$-module structure [def-weil-residue-field] compatible with the original $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ action through the residue map and with dimension one. For every $q\ge0$, $H^q(X,G)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is a finite $R$-module for the scalar action restricted along $f.\mathrm{appTop}$.

proof.text: The affine Noetherian base and proper finite-type source are Noetherian. Apply Chow to the integral closed subscheme W. Its modification is projective both over W and over the base, with a common relatively ample invertible module L.

Choose n with positive higher images of L^n under the modification zero. Set G = i_* pi_* L^n. Over affine opens of W, projective cohomology finiteness and quasi-coherent localization identify pi_* L^n with the sheaf associated to finite section modules, proving coherence independently of general proper coherence. Closed pushforward preserves coherence.

Leray for the modification, whose higher images vanish, identifies the cohomology of pi_* L^n with that of L^n. Closed pushforward identifies the cohomology of G with that of pi_* L^n. The latter is finite by projective cohomology finiteness over the affine base. These comparisons are linear for restriction of scalars along f.appTop.

At the generic point the modification is an isomorphism and L^n is invertible. Thus the generic stalk of G is a one-dimensional module over the residue field with the quotient scalar action; the maximal ideal acts by zero. Closed pushforward confines the support to i(W). This support is closed by coherence and contains the generic point, whose closure is i(W), so equality holds.
